T-2432 fitted the plate (the image store's 670 x 900 display copy) as a level view camera square to the front (yaw -90 in the footprint frame, u toward the street, v SOUTH on this side of the avenue: the eye looks east): the front's two edges, the downpipe at the party wall (x 140 px) and the south corner pier's outer face (x 433 px), are the 1911 sheet's 7.6 m front, 38.6 px/m at the front's plane, and grade at the front reads y 795 px. Its solve (eye 17.45 m out, 4.6 m south of the south wall, at 1.6 m; f 674, principal x 611) does not hold the south wall's level lines: the eave's shadow under the cornice runs straight from y 374 at the corner pier (x 434) to y 479.5 at x 522 (column profiles at x 438-522, slope 1.20), which on that camera climbs from 11.4 m at the front to 15.3 m at the rear section, and the heads of the two top-floor side windows (x 451, y 407; x 483, y 447) read 11.0 and 11.9 m. Solved instead by least squares on nine eave points and the two heads, each line level at its own height, and the 1911 sheet's depths (the rear section's corner 11.85 m back, at x 528 where the eave meets its cornice, y 486; its rear corner 7.6 m further back, x 608, where its lit south face meets the sky): the eye 28.7 m in front of the stone face and 8.39 m south of the south wall (u 48.15, v 15.99), f = 38.6 x 28.7 = 1108 px, so the principal point stands at x 757, off the plate's right edge (a view camera's shifted front, as its rise already put y off centre). The eye's height is the one number the lines leave soft (any height from 0.5 to 1.6 m fits them within 1 px). It is set at 1.0 m over the front's grade (horizon y 756), bounded by the rear section's door, whose dark runs down to the fence's top rail at y 779: grade at the rear section's face must stand at or under that, which an eye over about 1.3 m does not allow (at 1.6 m that grade reads y 776). The bound is about +-0.4 m on the eye's height, and moves heights read at the rear section by about +-0.15 m.
